title: Silent Config Loading Failures (The Ghost Default)
pattern: Suppressing file-system or parser errors during application startup, failing silently and falling back to default states without operator warning.
why_bad: An operator supplying a typo (e.g. `p0rt: 8080`) will find the system starts up anyway, but binds to a default port (like 80) or connects to a staging database instead of production, triggering catastrophic failures.
detection: Error suppression or `unwrap_or_default` calls inside configuration loading functions.
fix: Abruptly terminate execution (crash) on startup if any configuration file is missing, unreadable, or contains syntax/logical errors, returning actionable diagnostics.
source: Ousterhout, John K - *A Philosophy of Software Design* (2018_2019, Yaknyam Press).pdf, Section 8.2; Titus Winters, Tom Manshreck, Hyrum Wright - *Software Engineering at Google_ Lessons Learned from Programming Over Time* (2020, O'Reilly Media).pdf, Chapter 24.
